violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours: BEEF BONE BROTH AT 47F PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN DEEP SOUP POT IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE FOODS ARE COOLED FROM 135F TO 70F IN 2 HOURS AND TO A FURTHER 41F WITHIN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS USING PROPER COOLING METHODS.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: PORK BONE SOUP AT 111-115F ON COUNTER; BEEF BONE BROTH AT 118F, PORK BONE BROTH AT 121F, POTATO SOUP AT 118F ON STOVE TOP AND MIXED ENTRAILS AT 123 -132F ON COUNTER
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO REHEAT FOODS TO 165F OR ABOVE FOR HOT HOLDING AT 135F. FOODS WERE REHEATED: PORK BONE SOUP AT 178-196F; BEEF BONE BROTH AT 196-204F, PORK BONE BROTH AT 202F, POTATO SOUP AT 207F AND MIXED ENTRAILS AT 196-200F.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: BEEF BONE BROTH AT 47F PREPARED THE PREVIOUS DAY IN DEEP SOUP POT IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO DISCARD FOODS DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE ICE WANDS, SMALLER PORTIONS IN FREEZER OR REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL BROTHS OR SOUPS TO THE PROPER COOLING PARAMETERS.

violations.title: Where to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee was observed cleaning their hands in a MOP SINK.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands in ONLY a designated handsink. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO WASH HANDS AT HANDWASH SINK ONLY. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control (TPHC) with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): PORK BONE SOUP, CABBAGE SOUP, POTATO SOUP, PORK BONE BROTH, BEEF BONE BROTH ON CARTS IN KITCHEN ALL WITHIN ACCEPTABLE HOT HOLDING TEMPERATURES RANGES. PIC INDICATED FOODS WERE ON TIME TO BE DISCARDED AT SOME AT 2:00 PM AND OTHERS AT 3:00 PM. NO TIME LABELS OR DOCUMENTATION FOR TPHC PROCEDURES FOR FOODS WERE OBSERVED.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO PLACE 4 HOUR TIME LABLES ON FOODS DURING INSPECTION. EHS WILL FORWARD TO PIC DOCUMENTATION FOR FOODS USING TPHC PROCEDURES. Ko Hyang House (Inspection Date: 12/05/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name: SPRAY BOTTLES OF CLEANING CHEMICALS WITHOUT LABELS IN FRONT SERVICE AND BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO HAVE SPRAY BOTTLES LABELED DURING INSPECTION.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: RAW PORK FEET THAWING IN BUCKETS OF WATER OUTSIDE THE WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO TRANSFER MEATS TO WALK IN REFRIGERATOR TO COMPLETE THAWING DURING INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cold Holding

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: OBSERVED KIMCHI, BLOOD SAUSAGE PREPARED MORE THAN 24 HOURS WITHOUT DATE MARKING IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PIC APPLIED APPROPRIATE DATE MARKING DURING INSPECTION. PLEASE ENSURE CONTINUED COMPLIANCE. Ko Hyang House (Inspection Date: 06/06/2025) Page 2 of 3

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer GARLIC containers were observed reused for the storage of SALT, SUGAR AND PREPARED SAUCES ON COUNTERS AND IN WALK IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE TRANSFER FOODS TO FOOD SAFE NSF APPROVED CONTAINERS AND REFRAIN FROM REUSING MANUFACTURERS’ CONTAINERS FOR FOOD STORAGE. COMPLIANCE WILL BE CONFIRMED IN NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: BULK STORAGE ITEMS REMOVED FROM ORIGINAL PACKAGES SUCH AS MSG, SUGAR, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PLEASE PROVIDE LABELS FOR BULK STORAGE CONTAINERS.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. OBSERVED SEVERAL COOKED AND RAW FOODS: PORK BONE SOUP AND BROTH, VEGETABLES AND RAW PORK STORED DIRECTLY ON THE FLOOR IN THE WALK IN THE REFRIGERATOR AND IN THE BACK KITCHEN.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EDUCATION PROVIDED. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS TO STORE FOODS 6 INCHES ABOVE THE FLOOR.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: Milk crate(s) found used for the following purpose(s): STORE DRY GOODS AND SINGLE SERVICE ITEMS IN AREA OF ENTRANCE TO KITCHEN FROM DINING ROOM (TAKE OUT SERVICE AREA).
violations.corrective_action: Milk crates, soda crates, and/or bread racks are not designed to store or elevate food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, and single-service items. Provide only ANSI-certified (such as NSF-listed) shelving units, storage units, or dunnage racks. EDUCATION PROVIDED. PLEASE PROVIDE APPROVED SHELVING OR DUNNAGE RACKS BEFORE NEXT INSPECTION.
